mock_data.title: Bullying
mock_data.passage:
Education is a very important part of a child's life, and yet an increasing number of children are showing reluctance to attend school. It is not that they find the work too difficult or are afraid of the teachers. No, it is because they are being bullied.

School bullies can make other children's lives a misery and their bullying takes different forms. Often they will use their physical size to intimidate those who are smaller and weaker than themselves. They will threaten their victims with a beating if they don't do as they say, often using physical force to extort money, and will steal possessions from them by force.

Bullies use verbal abuse as well as physical abuse on their victims. The butt of this abuse may often simply be slightly different in some way from the rest of the class. A child may have red hair, wear spectacles, not have the latest fashion in shoes, have only one parent, or be of a different race, for example. This can make them a target for the school bully, who will indulge in the most insulting name-calling.

Some psychologists say that the desire of the class bully to dominate the others is a result of an inferiority complex or some personal unhappiness, but this does not help those who are on the receiving end of the abuse. So great is the bullying problem that many schools have been forced to draw up an official strategy for dealing with it.

Teachers encourage the victims of bullying to report the matter to one of them, but many of them are afraid to do so, for fear of more physical assault or more taunts. The bullies will accuse them of telling tales and make them suffer more. Furthermore, those who browbeat others, although domineering, can often appear to be charming to those who are in authority.

Because it is so difficult to get victims to report bullies, and often difficult to prove coercion, many bullies escape unpunished. We must protect our children from this persecution. They have a right to enjoy their schooldays.
mock_data.passageB1:
Going to school is very important for children. But more and more children don't want to go. It's not because the work is too hard, or they don't like the teachers. It's because they are being bullied.

School bullies can make life very bad for other children. Bullying can happen in different ways. Sometimes, bullies are bigger and stronger. They intimidate smaller children. They threaten to hurt them if they don't do what they say. Bullies might extort money or steal things from other children.

Bullies also use words to hurt people. They might verbally abuse other children. Sometimes, they pick on children who are a little different. Maybe a child has red hair, wears glasses, or doesn't have the newest clothes. Maybe they only have one parent, or they are from a different country. This can make them a target for bullies. Bullies will call them insulting names.

Some experts say that bullies want to be in charge because they feel bad about themselves. They might be unhappy. But this doesn't help the children who are being bullied. Bullying is such a big problem that many schools have a plan to deal with it.

Teachers tell children who are being bullied to report it to them. But many children are afraid to tell. They are scared they will get hurt or made fun of even more. Bullies might say they are telling tales and make them suffer more. Sometimes, bullies seem nice to teachers and other adults, even though they are domineering to other kids.

It's hard to get children to report bullies. It's also hard to prove that someone is being forced to do something. So, many bullies don't get punished. We need to protect children from bullying. They should be able to enjoy their time at school. They have a right to feel safe and happy.
mock_data.passageB2:
Education plays a crucial role in a child's development, yet a growing number of students are reluctant to attend school. This isn't always due to academic difficulties or fear of teachers. Instead, many children are experiencing bullying, which can have a devastating impact on their well-being.

Bullying in schools can take many forms, making victims' lives incredibly difficult. Bullies often exploit their physical advantage to intimidate smaller or weaker students. They might threaten violence if their demands aren't met, often resorting to physical force to extort money or steal possessions. This creates a climate of fear and insecurity for the targeted individuals.

Verbal abuse is also a common tactic employed by bullies. Victims are often targeted for being different in some way. This could be anything from having red hair or wearing glasses to not owning the latest clothes or having a different family structure. These perceived differences can make them a prime target for bullies, who may engage in hurtful name-calling and other forms of verbal harassment. These attacks can be deeply damaging to a child's self-esteem and confidence.

Some psychologists suggest that a bully's desire to dominate others stems from their own feelings of insecurity or personal unhappiness. While this might offer some insight into the bully's motivations, it doesn't lessen the pain and suffering experienced by the victims. The problem is so prevalent that many schools have been forced to develop formal policies to address it. These policies often include clear guidelines for reporting and addressing bullying incidents.

Teachers encourage students to report bullying, but many victims are afraid to come forward, fearing further retaliation or increased harassment. Bullies may accuse them of being "tattletales" and make their lives even more miserable. Furthermore, bullies can often be deceptive, appearing charming and well-behaved to adults while tormenting their peers. This makes it difficult to gather evidence and hold them accountable for their actions.

Because reporting bullying can be challenging, and proving it is often difficult, many bullies evade punishment. It is essential that we protect children from this form of persecution. They have the right to feel safe and secure at school and to enjoy their education without fear. Schools must work to create a supportive environment where bullying is not tolerated, and victims feel empowered to speak out and seek help. Raising awareness and promoting empathy are key steps in preventing bullying and fostering a more inclusive and respectful school community.
mock_data.passageC1:
The formative years spent in education are paramount, yet a growing number of students are displaying a marked aversion to attending school. This reluctance often doesn't stem from academic difficulty or apprehension towards educators. Instead, it frequently arises from the distressing phenomenon of bullying, a pervasive issue that casts a long shadow over the educational landscape.

School bullies can inflict considerable suffering on their peers, and their methods are manifold. A common tactic involves leveraging physical stature to intimidate those who are smaller or more vulnerable. Such individuals may resort to issuing veiled or explicit threats of physical violence should their demands – often involving the extortion of money or the forceful theft of possessions – not be met. This creates an atmosphere of fear and coercion.

Beyond physical aggression, bullies frequently employ verbal abuse, targeting perceived differences in their victims. These differences might encompass superficial characteristics such as hair color, the wearing of glasses, a lack of adherence to current fashion trends, the composition of their family (such as being raised by a single parent), or their racial or ethnic background. These superficial differences can render a child a target for relentless name-calling and demeaning remarks, perpetuating a cycle of abuse.

Some psychologists posit that the bully's desire to assert dominance over others is indicative of an underlying inferiority complex or some form of personal distress. However, such explanations offer little solace to those who are on the receiving end of the abuse. Indeed, the problem of bullying has become so acute that many educational institutions have been compelled to formulate comprehensive strategies for addressing it. While teachers encourage victims to report instances of bullying, many are hesitant to do so, apprehensive of further physical or verbal attacks. Bullies are apt to accuse them of being 'telltales,' thereby exacerbating their suffering. Furthermore, bullies, while domineering towards their victims, can often project an image of charm and compliance to those in positions of authority.

Given the difficulties inherent in persuading victims to report bullying and the challenges in substantiating claims of coercion, many perpetrators evade punishment. It is imperative that we shield our children from this form of persecution. They are inherently entitled to a positive and fulfilling experience during their school years, free from fear and intimidation. Schools need to implement more successful strategies in order to ensure that all children are able to thrive.

mock_data.translation:
Ta'lim bola hayotining juda muhim qismidir, ammo shunga qaramay, ko'payib borayotgan bolalar maktabga borishni xohlamayotganliklarini ko'rsatmoqdalar. Bu ularning o'qishini juda qiyin deb bilishlari yoki o'qituvchilardan qooshishlari bilan bog'liq emasi. Yo'q, buning sababi ularga nisbatan bezorilik qilinayotganidir (bullying).

Maktab bezorilari boshqa bolalarning hayotini azobga aylantirishi mumkin va ularning bezoriligi har xil shakllarda namoyon bo'ladi. Ko'pincha ular o'zlaridan kichikroq va kuchsizroq bo'lganlarni qo'rqitish (intimidate) uchun jismoniy kuchlaridan foydalanadilar. Ular o'z qurbonlarini (victims) agar aytganlarini qilmasalar, kaltaklash bilan qo'rqitadilar, ko'pincha pulni tovlamachilik yo'li bilan olish (extort) uchun jismoniy kuch ishlatadilar va ularning buyumlarini zo'ravonlik bilan o'g'irlaydilar.

Bezorilar o'z qurbonlariga nisbatan so'zlar bilan haqorat qilish (verbal abuse) va jismoniy zulm (physical abuse) ishlatadilar. Bu haqoratning nishoni (butt) ko'pincha sinfning qolgan qismidan biror jihati bilan biroz farq qiladigan bolalar bo'lishi mumkin. Masalan, bolaning sochlari qizil bo'lishi, ko'zoynak taqishi, poyabzalda so'nggi modada bo'lmasligi, faqat bitta ota-onasi bo'lishi yoki boshqa irqdan bo'lishi mumkin. Bu ularni maktab bezorilari uchun nishonga (target) aylantirishi mumkin, ular eng haqoratli laqab qo'yishlar (name-calling) bilan shug'ullanadilar.

Ba'zi psixologlarning ta'kidlashicha, sinf bezorisining boshqalarga hukmronlik qilish (dominate) istagi o'zini past ko'rish kompleksi (inferiority complex) yoki qandaydir shaxsiy baxtsizlik natijasidir, ammo bu haqoratning jabrlanuvchisi bo'lgan (on the receiving end) kishilarga yordam bermaydi. Bezorilik muammosi shunchalik kattaki, ko'plab maktablar unga qarshi kurashish uchun rasmiy strategiya tuzishga majbur bo'lishdi.

O'qituvchilar bezorilik qurbonlarini bu haqda xabar berishga undaydilar, ammo ularning ko'pchiligi jismoniy hujum (assault) yoki ko'proq pichinglardan (taunts) qo'rqib, bunday qilishga botinishmaydi. Bezorilar ularni chaqimchilikda (telling tales) ayblaydi va ularni ko'proq azoblashadi. Bundan tashqari, boshqalarni do'q-po'pisa qiladiganlar (browbeat), garchi hukmronlikka moyil (domineering) bo'lishsa-da, ko'pincha mansabdor shaxslarga jozibali ko'rinishi mumkin.

Qurbonlarni bezorilar haqida xabar berishga ko'ndirish qiyinligi va ko'pincha majburlashni (coercion) isbotlash qiyinligi sababli, ko'plab bezorilar jazolanmasdan qoladilar. Biz bolalarimizni ushbu zulmdan (persecution) himoya qilishimiz kerak. Ularning maktab davridan zavqlanishga haqlari bor.

right.uzbek: Sizga qilishga yoki ega bo'lishga ruxsat etilgan narsa.
right.example: Everyone has the right to an education.
right.definition: Something you are allowed to do or have.

steal.example: Someone tried to steal my bicycle.
steal.definition: To take something that doesn't belong to you.
steal.exampleUzbek: Kimdir mening velosipedimni o'g'irlashga harakat qildi.

extort.uzbek: Zo'ravonlik yoki tahdidlardan foydalanib, kimdandir bir narsa olish.
extort.example: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owners.
extort.definition: To get something from someone by using force or threats.
extort.exampleUzbek: Guruh do'kon egalaridan pul undirishga harakat qildi.

report.uzbek: Sodir bo'lgan narsa haqida kimdirga aytib berish.
report.example: You should report the crime to the police.
report.definition: To tell someone about something that has happened.
report.exampleUzbek: Siz jinoyat haqida politsiyaga xabar berishingiz kerak.

target.uzbek: Kimdir xafa qilishga yoki hujum qilishga harakat qilayotgan kimsa yoki narsa.
target.example: The small animal was an easy target for the hawk.
target.definition: Someone or something that someone is trying to hurt or attack.
target.exampleUzbek: Kichkina hayvon burgut uchun oson nishon edi.

bullied.uzbek: Kuchliroq yoki ko'proq hokimiyatga ega bo'lgan odam tomonidan xafa qilingan yoki qo'rqitilgan.
bullied.example: He was bullied at school because he was small.
bullied.definition: To be hurt or frightened by someone who is stronger or has more power.
bullied.exampleUzbek: U kichkinaligi sababli maktabda uni haqorat qilishgan.

bullies.uzbek: Boshqalarni, ayniqsa zaif odamlarni xafa qiladigan yoki qo'rqitadigan odamlar.
bullies.example: The school is trying to stop the bullies.
bullies.definition: People who hurt or frighten others, especially weaker people.

protect.uzbek: Kimnidir yoki biror narsani zarardan himoya qilish.
protect.example: We need to protect our children from danger.
protect.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm.
protect.exampleUzbek: Biz bolalarimizni xavfdan himoya qilishimiz kerak.

unhappy.example: She was unhappy because she missed her friends.
unhappy.exampleUzbek: U do'stlarini sog'ingani uchun xafa edi.

bullying.uzbek: Zaifroq odamni xafa qilish yoki qo'rqitish harakati.
bullying.example: Bullying is a serious problem in many schools.
bullying.definition: The act of hurting or frightening someone who is weaker.
bullying.exampleUzbek: Ko'pgina maktablarda bezorilik jiddiy muammo hisoblanadi.

threaten.uzbek: Agar ular siz xohlagan narsani qilmasa, kimnidir xafa qilishni aytish.
threaten.example: He threatened to tell my secrets if I didn't help him.
threaten.definition: To say you will hurt someone if they don't do what you want.
threaten.exampleUzbek: Agar men unga yordam bermasam, sirlarimni aytish bilan tahdid qildi.

insulting.example: He made some very insulting remarks.

intimidate.example: The bully tried to intimidate the younger children.
intimidate.exampleUzbek: Bezorilar yosh bolalarni qo'rqitishga harakat qilishdi.

domineering.uzbek: Boshqa odamlarni nazorat qilishga harakat qilish.

deal with it.uzbek: Muammoni hal qilish uchun chora ko'rish.
deal with it.example: The school has a plan to deal with bullying.
deal with it.definition: To take action to solve a problem.
deal with it.exampleUzbek: Maktabda bezorilikka qarshi kurashish rejasi mavjud.

verbally abuse.uzbek: Kimnidir xafa qilish yoki haqorat qilish uchun so'zlardan foydalanish.
verbally abuse.example: The coach verbally abused the players after the game.
verbally abuse.definition: To use words to hurt or insult someone.
verbally abuse.exampleUzbek: Murabbiy o'yindan keyin o'yinchilarni og'zaki haqorat qildi.

evade.example: He tried to evade the police.
evade.definition: To escape or avoid, especially by cleverness or trickery.

extort.example: The gang tried to extort money from the local businesses.
extort.definition: To obtain (something) by force, threats, or other unfair means.
extort.exampleUzbek: Guruh mahalliy korxonalardan pul shantaj qilmoqchi bo'ldi.

exploit.example: Companies exploit natural resources for profit.
exploit.definition: To make full use of and derive benefit from (a resource).
exploit.exampleUzbek: Kompaniyalar foyda olish uchun tabiiy resurslardan foydalanadi.

deceptive.definition: Giving an appearance or impression different from the true one; misleading.

prevalent.example: The disease is more prevalent in developing countries.
prevalent.definition: Widespread in a particular area or at a particular time; common.

reluctant.example: She was reluctant to admit she was wrong.
reluctant.exampleUzbek: U xato qilganini tan olishni istamadi.

insecurity.definition: The state of being open to danger or threat; lack of protection.
insecurity.exampleUzbek: Uning xavfsizligi yo'qligi uni rashkchi qildi.

tormenting.example: The bullies were tormenting the younger children.
tormenting.definition: Inflicting severe physical or mental suffering on.

persecution.example: They suffered persecution for their beliefs.
persecution.definition: Hostile or ill-treatment, especially because of race or political or religious beliefs.
persecution.exampleUzbek: Ular o'z e'tiqodlari uchun ta'qibga uchradilar.

retaliation.example: He feared retaliation from the gang.
retaliation.definition: Action taken in return for an injury or wrong; revenge.

prime target.example: Small cars are a prime target for theft.

deeply damaging.exampleUzbek: Janjal uning obro'siga juda zararli edi.

raising awareness.example: The campaign aims at raising awareness about climate change.
raising awareness.definition: The act of increasing public knowledge and understanding of an issue.
raising awareness.exampleUzbek: Kampaniya iqlim o'zgarishi haqida xabardorlikni oshirishga qaratilgan.

supportive environment.example: The school provides a supportive environment for students.

supportive environment.exampleUzbek: Maktab o'quvchilar uchun qo'llab-quvvatlovchi muhit yaratadi.

evade.uzbek: Qochish yoki qochish, ayniqsa aqlli yoki hiyla-nayrang bilan.
evade.example: He evaded the police for several weeks.
evade.definition: Escape or avoid, especially by cleverness or trickery.
evade.exampleUzbek: U bir necha hafta davomida politsiyadan qochib yurdi.

render.example: The rain rendered the roads impassable.

implement.uzbek: Qaror, reja, kelishuv va hokazolarni amalga oshirish.

mock_data.translationB1:
Maktabga borish bolalar uchun juda muhim. Ammo tobora ko'proq bolalar borishni xohlamayapti. Buning sababi ish juda qiyinligi yoki o'qituvchilar yoqmasligi emas. Buning sababi ularni bezorilik qilishmoqda.

Maktab bezorilari boshqa bolalarning hayotini juda yomonlashtirishi mumkin. Bezorilik turli yo'llar bilan sodir bo'lishi mumkin. Ba'zan, bezorilar kattaroq va kuchliroq bo'ladi. Ular kichikroq bolalarni qo'rqitadi. Agar ular aytganini qilmasa, ularga zarar yetkazish bilan tahdid qiladi. Bezorilar pul talab qilishi yoki boshqa bolalardan narsalarni o'g'irlashi mumkin.

Bezorilar odamlarga zarar yetkazish uchun so'zlardan ham foydalanadi. Ular boshqa bolalarni og'zaki haqorat qilishi mumkin. Ba'zan, ular biroz farq qiladigan bolalarni tanlaydi. Ehtimol, bolaning sochlari qizil, ko'zoynak taqadi yoki eng so'nggi kiyimlari yo'qdir. Ehtimol, ularning faqat bitta ota-onasi bor yoki ular boshqa davlatdan kelgan. Bu ularni bezorilar uchun nishonga aylantirishi mumkin. Bezorilar ularni haqoratli ismlar bilan ataydi.

Ba'zi ekspertlarning aytishicha, bezorilar o'zlarini yomon his qilganlari uchun boshqaruvda bo'lishni xohlashadi. Ular xafa bo'lishi mumkin. Ammo bu bezorilikka uchrayotgan bolalarga yordam bermaydi. Bezorilik shunchalik katta muammoki, ko'plab maktablarda unga qarshi kurashish rejasi mavjud.

O'qituvchilar bezorilikka uchrayotgan bolalarga bu haqda ularga xabar berishni aytishadi. Ammo ko'plab bolalar aytishga qo'rqadi. Ular yana ham ko'proq zarar ko'rishdan yoki masxara qilinishdan qo'rqishadi. Bezorilar ular gap tashiyotganini aytishi va ularga yanada ko'proq azob berishi mumkin. Bu istaksizlik ko’pincha akademik qiyinchilik yoki o’qituvchilarga nisbatan qo’rquvdan kelib chiqmaydi. Aksincha, u ko’pincha ta’lim muhitiga uzoq soya soladigan keng tarqalgan muammo – bullingning achinarli hodisasidan kelib chiqadi.

Maktab bullilari o’z tengdoshlariga jiddiy azob berishi mumkin va ularning usullari ko’p xilma-xildir. Keng tarqalgan taktika - kichikroq yoki zaifroq bo’lganlarni qo’rqitish uchun jismoniy qomatdan foydalanish. Bunday shaxslar, talablari – ko’pincha pul to’lash yoki mulkni kuch bilan o’g’irlash – bajarilmasa, jismoniy zo’ravonlik bilan yashirin yoki aniq tahdidlar qilishlari mumkin. Bu qo’rquv va majburlash muhitini yaratadi.

Jismoniy tajovuzdan tashqari, bullilar ko’pincha o’z qurbonlaridagi ko’rinadigan farqlarni nishonga olib, og’zaki haqorat qilishadi. Bu farqlar soch rangi, ko’zoynak taqish, hozirgi moda tendentsiyalariga rioya qilmaslik, ularning oilasi tarkibi (masalan, yolg’iz ota-ona tomonidan tarbiyalanish) yoki irqiy yoki etnik kelib chiqishi kabi yuzaki xususiyatlarni o’z ichiga olishi mumkin. Bu yuzaki farqlar bolani tinimsiz laqablar va kamsituvchi so’zlar uchun nishonga aylantirishi, suiiste’mollik tsiklini davom ettirishi mumkin.

Ba’zi psixologlarning ta’kidlashicha, bullining boshqalar ustidan hukmronlik qilish istagi uning yashirin past baholilik kompleksi yoki shaxsiy azoblanishning bir qanday shaklidan dalolat beradi. Biroq, bunday izohlar suiiste’molga uchrayotganlarga hech qanday tasalli bermaydi. Haqiqatan ham, bulling muammosi shunchalik keskinlashdiki, ko’plab ta’lim muassasalari uni hal qilish uchun keng qamrovli strategiyalarni ishlab chiqishga majbur bo’lishdi. O’qituvchilar qurbonlarni bulling holatlari haqida xabar berishga undashsa-da, ko’pchilik bundan tortinishadi, chunki ular keyingi jismoniy yoki og’zaki hujumlardan qo’rqishadi. Bullilar ularni "chaqimchilar" deb ayblashga moyil bo’lib, shu bilan ularning azobini kuchaytiradi. Bundan tashqari, bullilar o’z qurbonlariga nisbatan hukmronlik qilsalar ham, hokimiyat vakillariga nisbatan jozibali va itoatkor qiyofa yaratishlari mumkin.

Qurbonlarni bulling haqida xabar berishga ko’ndirishdagi qiyinchiliklar va majburlash da’volarini asoslashdagi muammolarni hisobga olgan holda, ko’plab aybdorlar jazodan qochib qutuladilar. Biz farzandlarimizni bu shakldagi ta’qiblardan himoya qilishimiz shart. Ular maktab yillarida qo’rquv va qo’rqitishdan xoli, ijobiy va to’laqonli tajribaga haqli. Barcha bolalar gullab-yashnashi uchun maktablar yanada muvaffaqiyatli strategiyalarni amalga oshirishi kerak.
